item.text:
The core \(n=2,3\) ceiling argument appears mathematically sound, including the wild primes, but the package as stated contains one false unconditional theorem and several unacknowledged classical dependencies.

1. Pinned left-edge shortcut

> “\(k > y_1+s_r\)”  
> “the true hull has a vertex at \((1,y_1)\)”

Classification: UPHELD.

Once (C1) holds, the resolved hull on \([1,n]\) is the true hull there. Because all roots and the center are integral, its slopes are nonnegative, so its heights do not exceed \(y_1\). Every completion has \(v(g_0)\ge k>y_1+s_r\), including \(g_0=0\). Thus \((1,y_1)\) remains a strict vertex in every completion, and its new left side has length one and slope \(>s_r,\lambda_{\rm prev}\). Its unique root is Galois-fixed and rational.

The mechanism is genuinely stable under all lifts: completions may change that rational root’s exact valuation, but cannot change its type \((1,1)\), the already-determined right hull, or the residual data read below \(k\).

The case-(b) read level is also correct:

> “\(k=y(1)+\lfloor b_2\rfloor+1\)”  
> “\(y(0)\ge k\)”

If \(b_1<\infty\), the length-one side makes \(b_1\in\mathbf Z\), and \(b_1>b_2\) gives \(b_1\ge\lfloor b_2\rfloor+1\). If \(b_1=\infty\), then \(y(0)=\infty\). Fractional \(b_2\) causes no problem because \(\lfloor b_2\rfloor+1>b_2\).

2. REC and the \(z_0=0\) corner

> “if \(z_0=0\) then \(c'=c\) and steeper-side roots keep \(v(\alpha-c')>h\)”  
> “the count in SIDE(ii) is exact either way”

Classification: JUSTIFICATION GAP.

As written, that reasoning is invalid: if \(z_0=0\), all roots on steeper sides would also satisfy \(v(\alpha-c')>h\), contradicting the claimed exact count \(m'\).

The theorem is rescued by an unstated observation already implicit in RES: the scaled slope factor \(G\) has unit roots, hence a unit constant coefficient, so \(\bar G(0)\ne0\). Since \(R\) is a nonzero scalar multiple of \(\bar G\), zero cannot be a residual root at all. Thus the bad corner is impossible—but the supplied REC proof does not cleanly establish this and contains a false “either way” assertion.

3. Order-\(\le1\) arithmetic for \(n\le3\)

> “a repeated residual factor on a side with \(e\ge2\) needs side length \(e\cdot d\ge4>n\)”

Classification: UPHELD for \(n=2,3\).

A residual factor can repeat only when the residual degree \(d\ge2\). If the slope denominator \(e\ge2\), its side length is \(ed\ge4\), impossible in total degree at most three. Therefore:

- \(e\ge2\) forces \(d=1\), so SIDE(i) closes the branch.
- Recursion can occur only on integral slopes \(e=1\).
- Refinement does not change the degree bound.
- No tame assumption enters, so \(p=2,3\) introduces no missing branch.

The package’s recurring phrase “\(n\le3\)” technically overstates Theorem N3, which is written only for \(2\le n\le3\). Degree one is trivial, but it is not covered by the stated theorem.

4. Ceiling and wild corners

> “\(L(f)\le v_p(\operatorname{disc}f)+1\)”

Classification: UPHELD for \(n=2,3\), subject to the REC gap above.

In case \(b_1=b_2\),

\[
b_1+b_2\le2\delta_{12},\qquad b_j\le\delta_{2j},
\]

and hence

\[
y(0)\le2\delta_{12}+\sum_{j\ge3}\delta_{2j}
\le2\sum_{i<j}\delta_{ij}=v_p(\operatorname{disc}f).
\]

In case \(b_1>b_2\), strict ultrametricity gives \(\delta_{12}=b_2\), while the vertex at index one gives \(y(1)=\sum_{j\ge2}b_j\). Therefore

\[
k-1=y(1)+\lfloor b_2\rfloor
\le2b_2+\sum_{j\ge3}b_j
\le v_p(\operatorname{disc}f).
\]

All inequality directions are correct.

For inseparable reduction, the discriminant reduces to zero, so a separable characteristic-zero polynomial has \(v_p(\operatorname{disc}f)\ge1\). Step 0’s read level \(1\) therefore satisfies the ceiling. This remains valid at wild \(p=2\) and \(p=3\); no division by \(2\), \(3\), or a tame ramification index occurs.

The termination argument is adequate: recursive levels are strictly increasing integers and are bounded by a pairwise root-distance valuation, hence ultimately by the finite discriminant valuation.

5. Envelope arithmetic

For N3:

> “\(\Gamma(v)=v+1\) (so \(\Gamma^{-}(N)=N\))”

Classification: UPHELD.

Indeed,

\[
\min\{v\ge0:v+1>N\}=N,
\]

so undecided separable inputs at level \(N\) must have \(v_p(\operatorname{disc}f)\ge N\). Applying I-TAIL with \(m=N\) gives exactly the displayed N3 envelope. The factor \(n-1\), ceiling, and \(w=n\,v_p(n)\) are substituted correctly.

But the general TR-Q statement says:

> “Let \(\Gamma\) be nondecreasing…”  
> “\(\Gamma^{-}(N):=\min\{v:\Gamma(v)>N\}\)”  
> “\(\Gamma^{-}(N)\to\infty\) since each \(\Gamma(v)\) is finite.”

Classification: CRITICAL ERROR.

Finite-valued and nondecreasing does not imply unbounded. For example, \(\Gamma(v)=1\) is finite and nondecreasing, but for \(N\ge1\) the defining set is empty, so \(\Gamma^{-}(N)\) is undefined. The assertion that it tends to infinity is false under the stated hypotheses.

This does not damage N3-ENV because \(\Gamma(v)=v+1\) is unbounded, but it falsifies TR-Q as advertised in the status table and its claimed general-\(n\) conditional formulation.

6. Undisplayed inputs

> “§3 must stand on Facts NP/SF/HEN alone.”

Classification: JUSTIFICATION GAP / OVERSTATEMENT.

The proof also consumes:

- the denominator-of-valuation divides the ramification index;
- \([K:\mathbf Q_p]=ef\) and the associated degree bound;
- the Gauss valuation’s associated graded ring being a domain;
- multiplicativity of initial forms;
- unit constant term for a monic polynomial whose roots are units;
- the correspondence between Hensel factors and root groups;
- the discriminant/root-difference identity (D);
- basic Galois invariance and uniqueness of the extended valuation.

These are standard classical facts, and none looks false, but they are not consequences of NP/SF/HEN alone and several are merely asserted inside RES or SIDE. Thus the claim of complete dependence only on the three displayed facts is inaccurate. I-TAIL is also an explicit named external import, as acknowledged.

Nothing in the mathematical N3 proof appears to consume AGR, CU-*, GD-\(\ge2\), GMN termination, or BNS. The as-built-engine conclusions remain properly conditional.

7. Rescope and numerics

The bracket display has the correct directions:

\[
U^{\rm sem}_N\subseteq U^{\rm can}_N
\subseteq\{v_p(\operatorname{disc})\ge N\}
=U^K_{2N-1}.
\]

The original proposed upper bound by a later-level semantic undecided set runs against the semantic-floor direction and is not established. The Krasner replacement is mathematically faithful, although the prose saying canonical is “at least as fast as” the semantic optimum is backwards or, at best, misleading: the semantic classifier has no more undecided classes than the canonical one.

The sealed numeric claims cannot be independently verified from this no-repository audit. They are not needed for the proof.

VERDICT: UNSOUND
